decisions.decision: Version forecasting data in a dedicated repository
decisions.context: Forecasts must be reproducible for any past week, so the training data used for each run needs a versioned reference. The design space compares dedicated data versioning with storing versioning alongside code and no data versioning (d:11).

alternatives.label: Data versioning in code repository
cons: May couple data workflow to code

decisions.rationale: A dedicated data version repository directly supports recovering the inputs for historical weekly runs (d:11, v:11.1). The design-point check returned no warnings, but no attesting sources; the combination is novel in this workspace.
consequences: Record the data version with each forecast run.
Maintain and operate data versioning alongside code.

decisions.decision: Process weekly demand data in batches
decisions.context: The retailer produces forecasts per store and product on a weekly cadence. The design space offers batch and real-time stream processing (d:15).
decisions.rationale: A weekly batch aligns processing with the stated forecast cadence without introducing a real-time requirement (d:15, v:15.1). The design-point check returned no warnings, but no attesting sources; the combination is novel in this workspace.
consequences: Schedule processing around the weekly run.
Late-arriving data needs a rerun or correction policy.

decisions.decision: Automate data preparation in a pipeline
decisions.context: Weekly runs need repeatable processing, while the three-person team needs a workflow that can be rerun as model ideas change. The design space compares a data pipeline with ETL, a dedicated component, and no automation (d:14).
decisions.rationale: A dedicated flexible pipeline makes recurring data preparation repeatable and supports rapid model iteration (d:14, v:14.1). The design-point check returned no warnings, but no attesting sources; the combination is novel in this workspace.
consequences: Pipeline changes need review and maintenance.

decisions.decision: Build and evaluate models in an automated pipeline
decisions.context: New model ideas should reach production quickly without disrupting the weekly run. The design space contrasts an automated model-building pipeline with a dedicated component and development-tool-only model building (d:18).
decisions.rationale: Automating training, evaluation, and validation provides a repeatable path from an experiment to a production candidate (d:18, v:18.1). The design-point check returned no warnings, but no attesting sources; the combination is novel in this workspace.
consequences: Promote candidates through a controlled release step.
Maintain pipeline definitions as model workflows evolve.

decisions.context: The system forecasts weekly demand and must reproduce past forecasts. The design space compares batch, incremental, and hybrid learning (d:19).

alternatives.label: Incremental learning
cons: Harder to recreate prior model state

decisions.rationale: Scheduled batch training matches the weekly cadence and provides a clear training run to associate with each model version (d:19, v:19.1). The design-point check returned no warnings, but no attesting sources; the combination is novel in this workspace.
consequences: Retrain on a defined schedule or approved data update.
Record the training data version with each model.

decisions.decision: Use CI/CD to deliver pipeline changes
decisions.context: The team wants model ideas to reach production quickly while protecting the weekly run. The design space distinguishes CI/CD from deployment scripts and no delivery automation (d:8), and identifies pipeline components as deployable artifacts (d:25).
decisions.rationale: Use CI/CD to build, test, and deploy the ML pipelines and components needed for pipeline runs (d:8, v:8.1; d:25, v:25.2). The checked design point produced no warnings, but no attesting sources; the combination is novel in this workspace.
consequences: Keep production promotion controlled to protect the weekly run.
